scenario: AITA for not ending my friendship with my best friend after he cheated on my sister? | Both my best friend and my sister know about my other account so this is a throwaway. I'm an 18 year old guy and I have a twin sister. I've been best friends with my best friend (we'll call him G) since kindergarten, so G and my sister have always been pretty close too. They've kind of had a "thing" going on our whole lives. For the longest time, they never officially dated for a bunch of different reasons I won't get into, but they were always really close and really into each other. A little over a year ago, when we were all 17, they finally started dating. Everything went really well for like 13 months, but then long story short, G cheated on my sister and I was the one who figured it out. He swore it wouldn't happen again and begged me not to tell my sister but I told her anyway. I was mad at him and he was mad at me so we didn't talk for a month and a half, which was honestly the weirdest month and a half of my whole life. G's practically like my brother, we've been inseparable since kindergarten, so not having him around was kinda....unbearable honestly lol After our streak of not talking to each other, G invited me on his family ski trip as a way to make amends (I've been on lots of his family's ski trips through the years). I accepted and ended up forgiving him and letting him back into my life because it was way too weird without him in it. I can tell he's genuinely sorry about what happened. He literally cried cause he felt so bad and I've only seen him cry like once before in my whole life Anyway, G and my sister broke up as soon as she found out he cheated and they're still not on speaking terms, so my sister obviously isn't happy about the whole situation. She's making me feel like shit for still being friends with G, and she doesn't seem to understand how big of a deal it would be for us to lose our 13 year friendship over her. I know G made a huge mistake, I hate him for it and I'll never 100% get over it, but I'm not gonna let it ruin my best and longest friendship. I think about it like this: if your best friend cheated on their SO and then felt like shit, would you end your friendship with them? No. So why is this any different just because his SO happened to be my sister? G and I are going to the same college in the fall (a different college in a different state than the one my sister's going to), so none of this is gonna be something that we even think about when we're living in different places Am I the asshole?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what's going on here. There's this guy, let's call him G, who's been my best friend since kindergarten. My twin sister and G have always been really close, almost like they had a "thing" going on, but they never officially dated for a long time. Then, when we were all 17, they finally started dating, and everything was great for about 13 months. But then, G cheated on my sister. I found out about it and told her, even though G begged me not to. I was mad at him, and he was mad at me, so we didn't talk for a month and a half. That was really weird and hard for me because G is like my brother, and not having him around felt unbearable. After that, G invited me on his family ski trip to make amends, and I accepted. I ended up forgiving him and letting him back into my life because it was too weird without him. I can tell he's genuinely sorry, and he even cried because he felt so bad. Now, G and my sister broke up right after she found out he cheated, and they're still not speaking. My sister is making me feel like shit for still being friends with G, and she doesn't understand why I wouldn't end our 13-year friendship over this. I know G made a huge mistake, and I hate him for it, but I don't want to lose my best friend over this. I think about it like this: if my best friend cheated on their significant other and felt bad about it, would I end our friendship? No, so why is this any different just because his SO happened to be my sister? G and I are going to the same college in the fall, so this might not even be an issue when we're living in different places. Am I the asshole for not ending my friendship with G after he cheated on my sister? Alright, so I need to figure out if I'm being unreasonable or if my sister is being too harsh. Let's break this down. First, G cheated on my sister, which is a serious betrayal. My sister is understandably hurt and angry, and she's taking it out on me for still being friends with G. On the other hand, I've known G for 13 years, and he's practically like my brother. Losing that friendship would be really hard for me, and I can see why I wouldn't want to do that. Plus, G seems genuinely sorry, and he's made an effort to make things right, like inviting me on the ski trip. But then, my sister feels like I'm not taking her side, and she's making me feel bad about it. Is it fair for her to expect me to cut off a friendship that's been so important to me? Or is she just being too sensitive? I mean, I get that she's hurt, but I also think that friendships can survive mistakes, especially when the person is truly sorry and has made an effort to fix things. Another thing to consider is the future. G and I are going to the same college, so we'll be seeing each other a lot. If I cut him out now, it might cause more problems down the line. Plus, we're both moving to different states, so maybe this whole situation will just fade away as we start our new lives. It's possible that in a few years, this won't even be a big deal anymore. But then again, my sister is my twin, and our relationship is really important too. I don't want to lose her over this either. It's a tough spot to be in because I care about both of them deeply. I guess I need to figure out what's more important: my friendship with G or my relationship with my sister. But that feels like a lose-lose situation because both are important to me. Maybe there's a middle ground. I could still be friends with G but set some boundaries to make sure my sister feels respected. That way, I'm not completely cutting him out, but I'm also acknowledging her feelings. It might help to talk to her about why I'm choosing to stay friends with G and see if we can find a compromise that works for both of us. I also wonder if there's a way to help G and my sister reconcile, but that seems unlikely since they're not even speaking. Maybe time will help heal the wound, but I don't know. It's a complicated situation, and I'm not sure what the right thing to do is. I just want everyone to be happy and not feel like they're losing someone they care about. In the end, I think I have to make the decision that feels right for me, even if it upsets my sister. I value my friendship with G, and I don't want to lose that over something that happened in the past, especially if he's shown that he's sorry and willing to make changes. But I also don't want to hurt my sister or make her feel like I don't care about her feelings. It's a tough spot, but I think I have to stand by my decision and hope that my sister can understand that I'm trying to do what's best for everyone involved.
